Rashi on Chullin 31b:12:1.hebrew: רבי יוחנן - דאמר לעיל: אף לביתה לא טהרה:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:12:1.english: Rabbi Yohanan - Who said above: "Even for her home she has not become pure."

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:1.hebrew: נגעי בגדים כתיב בהו ב' כבוסים: תכבוסת ראשונה, "וכבסו את אשר בו הנגע והסגירו וגו'" - לראות אם יפשה או יעמוד או יכהה. וכיבוס שני לאחר הסגר שאחר כיבוס ראשון: "והבגד או השתי או הערב או כל כלי העור אשר תכבס" - בראשונה קודם הסגר, "וסר מהם הנגע" - בימי הסגר, "וכובס שנית" - לשום טבילה, "וטהר":
Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:1.english: Regarding the plagues of garments, two launderings are written: The first laundering: "And they shall wash that in which is the plague, and shut it up, etc." (Leviticus 13:54), to see whether it spreads, or stays, or fades. And the second laundering is after the quarantine that follows the first laundering: "And the garment, or the warp, or the woof, or any article of skin, which you shall wash" (Leviticus 13:58) - the first time, before the quarantine; "and the plague has departed from them" - during the days of quarantine; "it shall be washed a second time" - for the sake of immersion; "and it shall be pure."

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:2.hebrew: מה ת"ל שנית - פשיטא דשנית הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:2.english: Why does the verse say "a second time"? - It is obvious that it is a second [immersion]!

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:3.hebrew: מקיש תכבוסת שנייה - שהיא לשם טבילת טהרה:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:3.english: He compares the second laundering - Which is for the sake of an immersion of purification:

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:4.english: For the first laundering - Which is for the quarantine.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:5.hebrew: מה ראשונה לדעת - אדם, דכתיב "וצוה הכהן וכבסו":
Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:5.english: Just as the first [instance] requires intent - Of a person, as it is written: "And the priest shall command, and they shall wash" (Leviticus 13:54).

Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:6.hebrew: אף שניה לדעת - ולא שיפול במים מאליו:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:13:6.english: So too the second [immersion must be] with awareness - And not that [the object] fall into the water on its own:

Rashi on Chullin 31b:15:1.english: Did Rabbi Yoḥanan say - that non-sacred slaughter requires intention?

Rashi on Chullin 31b:17:1.hebrew: מדגלי רחמנא מתעסק בקדשים - שוחט קדשים שלא בכוונה, דפסולין, דכתיב "לרצונכם תזבחו", "לדעתכם זבוחו", בפ"ק (לעיל חולין יג.):
Rashi on Chullin 31b:17:1.english: The Merciful One has made clear [that] one who acts unintentionally with sacrificial animals - One who slaughters sacrificial animals without intent, [the slaughter] is invalid, as it is written, "You shall slaughter it for your acceptance" [meaning,] "You shall slaughter it with your awareness," in the first chapter (above, Chullin 13a).

Rashi on Chullin 31b:18:1.english: And the Rabbis - Who said above, "And the Sages disqualify."

Rashi on Chullin 31b:19:1.hebrew: זכנהו - נצחן, כלומר בזאת נראין דבריו מדבריהם:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:19:1.english: He vindicated them - He defeated them; that is, in this [matter] his words appear [stronger] than their words.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג וכלים דומיא דאדם מה אדם דבר כוונה הוא - אף כלים דקמיכוין להו אדם:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:1:1.english: This is the text [we] read: "And vessels are like a person; just as a person is a matter of intent" - So too vessels [only if] a person intends for them [to receive the water].

Rashi on Chullin 31b:21:1.hebrew: מתקינות - בודקות אותן בשעת וסתן, ומטבילות אותן בשעת טבילתן:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:21:1.english: Prepare - They examine them at the time of their menstrual period, and immerse them at the time of their immersion.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:1.hebrew: חרדלית של גשמים - זרם גשמים המקלח מן ההר בכח, ואין טובלין בו, דהנצוק והקטפרס אינו חיבור, ולא הוו מקוה דארבעים סאה, שהרי אין מ' סאה במקום אחד. ואף על פי שיש הרבה למטה ולמעלה, הא קתני אינו חיבור. חרדלית היינו קטפרס, מדרון. ורב האי גאון גריס "הרדלית", שבאין מדליו של הר:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:1.english: A ḥardalit of rainwater - A stream of rainwater that gushes down from the mountain with force, and one may not immerse in it, for [water in] a spout or a slope is not a connection, and they do not constitute a mikveh of forty se'ah, since there are not forty se'ah in one place. And even though there is a lot [of water] below and above, it is taught that it is not a connection. "Ḥardalit" is the same as "katapres," a steep slope. And Rav Hai Gaon reads "Hardalit," [meaning water] that comes from the [tall] peaks of the mountain.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:2.hebrew: נגזור ראשין אטו כיפין - דתנן: מטבילין כלים בראש הגל הנתלש מן הים והלך למרחוק ובא לארץ, נכנס אדם תחת ראשו ומקבלו, דהוי טבילה זו במחובר לקרקע:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:2.english: Should we decree [against immersion in] crests because of [immersion in] waves? - For we learned [in a mishna]: One may immerse utensils in the crest of a wave that was torn away from the sea and traveled a distance and came onto the land. [If] a person entered beneath its crest and caught it [the water], [the immersion is invalid,] since this immersion would be in [water] attached to the ground.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:3.hebrew: קמ"ל דלא גזרינן - לשון קושיא הוא, ו"דלא בעינן כוונה לחולין" מנלן:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:3:3.english: It teaches us that we do not decree - This is a phrase of challenge: and [the ruling] that "intention is not required for non-sacred food," from where do we know it?

Rashi on Chullin 31b:4:1.hebrew: ואין מטבילין בכיפין - שלא יזרוק כלים בכיפי הגל, דהיינו באמצעיתו שהוא עשוי ככיפה. וטעמא, כדמפרש, מפני שהיא טבילת אויר, ואין מטבילין באויר:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:4:1.english: And one may not immerse [vessels] on the tops - That one should not throw vessels onto the "tops" of the heap [of water], that is, onto its middle, which is shaped like a dome. And the reason, as [the Gemara] explains, is that this is immersion in the air, and one may not immerse in the air.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:5:1.hebrew: ידיו טהורות - דלא בעינן כוונה לחולין:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:5:1.english: His hands are pure - For we do not require intent for [the ritual purity of] unconsecrated food.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:5:2.hebrew: אינן בכי יותן - דלא אחשבה להך נפילה:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:5:2.english: They are not subject to "if it is put" - Because he did not intend [to have the produce wet by] this falling [into the water].

Rashi on Chullin 31b:6:1.hebrew: ואם בשביל שיודחו ידיו - נתכוין ליטול את הפירות מן המים:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:6:1.english: But if it was so that his hands would be rinsed - [i.e., if] he intended to take the fruits out of the water [and not to rinse his hands]:

Rashi on Chullin 31b:6:3.hebrew: ופירות הרי הן בכי יותן - ומקבלין טומאה מכאן ואילך, דאחשבה להך נפילת פירות ליטול ידיו בהגבהתן, והוה ליה משקה שסופו לרצון. ותנן מכשירין (פ"א מ"א): כל משקה שסופו לרצון, אע"פ שאין תחלתו לרצון, מכשיר:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:6:3.english: But the produce – "behold, it is [susceptible] as in 'if water be put'" - And [the produce] can receive impurity from this point onward, because he has [now] designated this falling of the produce for washing his hands through their being raised [in the water], and it is [thus] a liquid whose end is with the owner's approval. And we learned in Makhshirin (1:1): "Any liquid whose end is with approval, even though its beginning was not with approval, renders [produce] susceptible."

Rashi on Chullin 31b:7:1.hebrew: לחולין - לאכול חולין. הוחזק, נתכוין בשעת טבילה לכך:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:7:1.english: For chullin - To eat chullin [non-sacred food]. It is established [that] he intended this at the time of immersion.

Rashi on Chullin 31b:8:1.hebrew: הכי קאמר - לעולם חולין לא בעו כוונה, והאי דתנא בהו "הוחזק", דאיצטריך לאשמועינן דאע"ג דאיכוין לטבילת טהרה, לא הויא כוונת חולין כוונה למעשר:
Rashi on Chullin 31b:8:1.english: This is what [the mishna] is saying - Certainly, [immersion for] ordinary food does not require intention. And as for the fact that [the mishna] taught about them "it was established," this was necessary to teach us that even though he intended [the immersion] for ritual purification, the intention of [immersing for] ordinary food is not considered intention with respect to [food designated as] tithe.

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:10:1.hebrew: הוא סבר דיחויי קא מדחי ליה נפק דק ואשכח דתניא כו' - וא"ת, אמאי סבר דמדחי ליה? והלא כבר זה דקדק מן המשנה דקתני ידיו טהורות, ומה מדקדק יותר מברייתא זו? וי"ל, דיש חילוק בין טבילת כל גופו לנטילת ידים, דטבילת גופו חמירא טפי. וכן צריך לומר בסמוך דפריך מסתם משנה לר' יוחנן, ומשני דשחיטה אפילו ר' יוחנן מודה, ואכתי תקשי ליה משנה דמסכת מכשירין (פ"ד מ"ז) אלא טבילת ידים שאני:
Tosafot on Chullin 31b:10:1.english: He thought he was merely deflecting him; he went out, examined, and found that it was taught, etc. - And if you ask: Why did he think that [Rav Nachman] was deflecting him? Did he not already derive this from the Mishnah, which teaches "his hands are pure"? What more does he derive from this baraita? And one can answer that there is a distinction between immersion of one's whole body and washing of the hands, for immersion of one's body is more stringent. And so one must say below, where [Rava] objects from an unattributed Mishnah against R. Yochanan, and [the Gemara] answers that regarding slaughter even R. Yochanan agrees; and still, the Mishnah of tractate Makhshirin (4:7) would be difficult for him, [and one must say] rather that immersion of the hands is different.

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:18:1.hebrew: נהי דלא בעינן כוונה לזביחה - פירוש, להתירה בזביחה זו לחתיכה מיהא בעינן. פירוש, לחתיכת סימנים, כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Chullin 31b:18:1.english: Granted that we do not require intent for the slaughtering (zevihah) - Meaning, to permit it by this slaughter, for the cutting at least we do require [intent]. Meaning, for the cutting of the signs (the windpipe and gullet), as I explained.

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:2:1.hebrew: וכי תימא ביושב ומצפה מאי למימרא - פירוש, אי אמרת בשלמא דלא מיירי ביושב ומצפה אלא סתמא כדקתני, א"ש, דמשמע דאשמועינן דחולין לא בעו כוונה. אבל אי איכא למידחי דאיירי ביושב ומצפה, מאי למימרא? דליכא למימר דאתא לאשמועינן דבעו כוונה, דהא לא משמע מיניה דאיירי ביושב ומצפה, דסתמא קתני ונפל, דמשמע טפי בלא יושב ומצפה. והרי"ך פירש, מאי למימרא דליכא למימר דאתא לאשמועינן דבעו כוונה, דהא קתני טהורה, משמע דקולא אתא לאשמועינן:
Tosafot on Chullin 31b:2:1.english: And if you say [that it refers to one who] sits and waits, what is the point of stating it? - Its explanation: Granted, if you say that it is not speaking of one who sits and waits but rather [it speaks] generally, as it teaches, it is well, for it implies that it teaches us that unconsecrated food (chullin) does not require intention. But if it is possible to reject this and [say] that it is speaking of one who sits and waits, what is the point of stating it? For it cannot be said that it comes to teach us that they do require intention, since it does not imply that it is speaking of one who sits and waits, for it teaches generally, "and it fell," which implies more [that it is] without sitting and waiting. And the Rei"kh explained: What is the point of stating it? For it cannot be said that it comes to teach us that they do require intention, since it teaches "it is pure," which implies that it comes to teach us a leniency.

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:3:1.hebrew: גזירה משום חרדלית של גשמים - פירש בקונטרס: ואין טובלין בחרדלית, משום דתנן (טהרות פ"ח מ"ט): הנצוק והקטפרס אין חיבור, ואין כאן מ' סאה במקום אחד, אע"פ שיש הרבה למעלה ולמטה. ובחנם פירש כן, דאפילו יש כמה סאין באותו מדרון, אסור לטבול בו, דמקוה אינו מטהר בזוחלין, כדתניא בת"כ: אך מעין ובור וגו', אי מה מעין מטהר בזוחלין אף מקוה כו', ת"ל אך מעין ובור: מעין מטהר בזוחלין, ומקוה באשבורן. ובקונטרס הביאה פרק במה אשה (שבת דף סה: ד"ה וסבר):
Tosafot on Chullin 31b:3:1.english: A decree because of a channel (ḥardalit) of the rains - Rashi explained: One may not immerse in a ḥardalit, because we learned in a mishnah (Teharot 8:9): "The [water] that pours down and the [water] of the katafres are not [considered] connected," and there are not forty se'ah here in one place, even though there is much above and below. But he explained this needlessly, for even if there are many se'ah on that slope, it is forbidden to immerse in it, since a mikveh does not purify in flowing water, as it was taught in Torat Kohanim: "Only a spring and a pit, etc." (Leviticus 11:36) – 'Might it be that just as a spring purifies in flowing water, so too a mikveh, etc.?' Therefore Scripture says, "Only a spring and a pit": a spring purifies in flowing water, but a mikveh [only] when it is gathered (ashboran). And Rashi cited this in the chapter Bameh Ishah (Shabbat 65b, s.v. ve-savar).

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:4:1.english: For we learned: One may immerse in the crests (rashin) - This is somewhat puzzling: if it is a Mishnah, why does it need to teach us twice "one may immerse in the crests (rashin)"? Perhaps that [Mishnah] "one may immerse in the crests" speaks of Torah law, similar to "one may not immerse in waves (kipin)," which is Torah law; and in the case of a wave that was detached (gal shenitlash), it teaches us that we do not decree even rabbinically.

Tosafot on Chullin 31b:6:1.english: And the fruits, behold they are in "if water be put" (ki yuttan) - That is, after he lifted them out; for as long as they are attached to the water, they do not become susceptible [to impurity], as we learned in Massekhet Makhshirin (4:6): A niddah who was rinsing a radish in a cave-pool, it is pure; [if] she lifted it out, even with any amount [of water], it is impure. The explanation is that then they became susceptible. And as for what is stated in the first chapter of Pesachim (16a), that there are two verses regarding susceptibility [to impurity], one for detached [produce] and one for attached [produce], and both are needed: this refers to when they fell into attached [water], so that they become susceptible after he lifted them out. And even though at that point they are detached, nevertheless [the second verse] was needed because at the beginning of their adhering they were in attached water.
